Class WindowReactions

java.lang.Object
com.trevlar.menukit.window.WindowReactions
public final class WindowReactions extends Object
The fire-entry for reactive verbs — the one place a contents change is turned into a ReactiveHook invocation, going through the same WindowEngine cascade as every behavior and bounded by the same ReactionGuard.

Explicit verbs, not a guess

Insert and take are separate calls rather than one auto-classified entry, because the caller — a firing seam — knows the exact semantics the boundary can't recover: a hopper insert is unambiguously an insert; a click-swap is both a take of the old stack and an insert of the new (architecture Part 2 §6), so a swap-capable seam calls fireTake(Address, ItemStack, ItemStack, ReactCause, boolean) then fireInsert(Address, ItemStack, ItemStack, ReactCause, boolean). No lossy net-count heuristic is baked in here.

Two tiers

  • Server-authoritative (fireInsert(Address, ItemStack, ItemStack, ReactCause, boolean)/fireTake(Address, ItemStack, ItemStack, ReactCause, boolean), server=true) — resolves ON_INSERT/ON_TAKE (SERVER tier) and routes invocation through the ReactiveDispatch port, so MK-alone no-ops and MKC owns server-thread/transaction semantics.
  • Client-observed (server=false) — resolves the observed variants (CLIENT tier) and invokes directly; MK-alone capable, pure UI feedback, no authority, fires for created slots too.

"A rejected insert must NOT fire onInsert"

Upheld at the call site: a seam fires only after a mutation has committed (gating runs before and vetoes; reactions run after). A blocked interaction never reaches here.

The owed gap

The firing seams (which vanilla menu methods to intercept per menu type; the client synced-change detector) are the architecture's named owed implementation, verified in-game. This class is the boundary they call; it is complete and bounded now, so wiring a seam later is a single call.
